mainTopic: Praying while traveling (תפלת הדרך, הביננו, riding, direction of prayer, praying early) and the new משנה on מוסף and a חבר עיר
overview: The amud opens by finishing אביי's rule that a person should always include himself with the צבור, so תפלת הדרך is said in plural: 'lead us to peace.' The גמרא then covers when to say it, the measure of a פרסה, and whether you must stand. A story shows רב ששת standing anyway when it was easy: 'from being good, do not be called bad.' Next the גמרא explains how הביננו (a shortened עמידה that counts fully) differs from the emergency תפלה קצרה. It then rules that a rider prays sitting on his donkey, like רבי. A ברייתא teaches that everyone aims his heart, circle by circle, toward the קודש הקדשים, so all of Israel faces one place. The גמרא discusses praying early before a trip, and the tension between standing for the עמידה and keeping גאולה next to תפלה, including how רב אשי handled a busy day. Finally a new משנה brings three views on מוסף and a חבר עיר; the halacha follows רבי יהודה, and שמואל's supporting statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Always include yourself with the community
steps.stepSummary: אביי's rule (begun on the previous daf) ends: a person should join himself together with the צבור when he prays.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person should include himself together with the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's teaching that a person should always pray as part of the group, not only for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is said about תפלת הדרך. Even when one person is traveling alone, he should word his request as part of the whole community. The next steps show how this changes the actual words.

phrases.english: A person should include himself
phrases.notes: This finishes אביי's line from the previous daf, which opened with 'לעולם', always.

phrases.english: together with the congregation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's statement from the end of the previous daf about תפלת הדרך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When praying, a person should include himself with the צבור and not pray only for himself.

steps.title: How exactly should he word it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the actual words are when you include yourself with the צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: How should he say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question to set up the next step: what words show that you are including the group?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in step 1 is general. Here the גמרא wants the real wording, so we know how to keep the rule.

phrases.english: How should he say it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to put step 1's rule into practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording of תפלת הדרך that includes the community.

steps.title: Say it in plural: 'lead us to peace'
steps.stepSummary: The answer: 'May it be Your will, ה' our God, that You lead us to peace', using 'us' and not 'me'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'May it be Your will, ה' our God, that You lead us to peace,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opening words of תפלת הדרך and shows that they are in plural.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important point is the plural 'us' (שתוליכנו) and 'our God' (אלהינו). That is how a traveler, even alone, includes himself with the צבור.
steps.whatToRemember: תפלת הדרך is said in plural, 'that You lead us to peace', because a person should always include himself with the צבור.

phrases.english: 'May it be Your will, Lord our God,
that You lead us to peace,' etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ שֶׁתּוֹלִיכֵנוּ לְשָׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The prayer is said in plural: 'that You lead us to peace'.

steps.title: When does one say תפלת הדרך?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks at what point one should say תפלת הדרך.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does one pray it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a set of practical questions about תפלת הדרך. This first one asks about timing, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know the wording, the גמרא moves to practical details. The question is whether you say it before leaving or once you are already on the road.

phrases.english: When does one pray it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from wording to practical details of the same prayer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The time when תפלת הדרך is said.

steps.title: Once you are actually on the road
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב in the name of רב חסדא: from when one is already walking on the road.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said in the name of רב חסדא: from the time he is walking on the road.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that you say תפלת הדרך once you have started the trip, not while you are still at home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayer is for someone who is actually traveling. So it starts once the journey has begun, and not while he is only planning to leave.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said that Rav Ḥisda said:
From the time he is walking on the road.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁמְּהַלֵּךְ בַּדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One says it once he has set out on the road.

steps.title: How much distance is involved?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks 'up to how much?', a question about the distance connected to the prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second practical question, about distance. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is very short, so it can be read in more than one way. See the next step for the answer and how it is understood.

keyTerms.meaning: up to how much / how far

phrases.english: Up to how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second practical question following the timing question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The distance that matters for תפלת הדרך.

steps.title: The measure is one פרסה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב in the name of רב חסדא: the measure is a פרסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said in the name of רב חסדא: up to a פרסה.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer gives a measure of distance: one פרסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same chain, רבי יעקב in the name of רב חסדא, gives this answer too. The measure of a פרסה sets the limit for this prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: a measure of distance, a parasang (several kilometers)

steps.confusionAlert: 'עד כמה' is read in two ways. One reading: the trip must be at least a פרסה long to need תפלת הדרך. Another reading: you can still say it until you have gone a פרסה into the trip.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said that Rav Ḥisda said:
Up to a parasang.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא עַד פַּרְסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The measure for תפלת הדרך is one פרסה.

steps.title: In what position is it said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the prayer is said: standing, or is walking fine?
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does one say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a third practical question, about body position. This sets up a מחלוקת in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A traveler is moving, so the question is whether he must stop and stand. The answer will be a disagreement between רב חסדא and רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: and how does he say it

phrases.english: And how does he recite it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third practical question about the prayer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether תפלת הדרך must be said standing.

steps.title: רב חסדא: only standing
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא holds the prayer is said standing still.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: standing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the traveler should stop and say the prayer standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב חסדא, standing still is the proper way to say תפלת הדרך, even though the person is in the middle of a trip.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said: Standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to step 8.

steps.title: רב ששת: even while walking
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת holds you may say it even while walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: even while walking.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת disagrees and says you do not have to stop; you can say it while walking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אפילו' (even) shows that for רב ששת standing is fine but not required. This matters for the story that follows.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: Even walking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב חסדא in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפלת הדרך may be said even while walking.

steps.title: Story: רב חסדא stops to pray on the road
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רב ששת were traveling together, and רב חסדא stood up to pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רב ששת were walking on the road. רב חסדא stood and prayed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story about the two אמוראים from the מחלוקת. רב חסדא follows his own view and stops to pray standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story puts both sides of the מחלוקת on the same road. The question is what רב ששת will do, since he holds that standing is not required.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda and Rav Sheshet
were walking along the road,
Rav Ḥisda stood and was praying.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת הֲווֹ קָאָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing how the two sides of the מחלוקת acted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא practiced his own view and stood to say תפלת הדרך.

steps.title: רב ששת asks what רב חסדא is doing
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks his attendant what רב חסדא is doing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to his attendant: What is רב חסדא doing?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת asks his attendant what is happening. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת was blind, so he could not see that רב חסדא had stopped. He asks so that he can decide what to do himself.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to his attendant:
What is Rav Ḥisda doing?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ מַאי קָא עָבֵיד רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רב חסדא is doing at that moment.

steps.title: The attendant: he is standing and praying
steps.stepSummary: The attendant answers that רב חסדא is standing and praying.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He is standing and praying.
steps.whatsHappening: The attendant tells רב ששת that רב חסדא has stopped and is praying standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רב ששת knows that רב חסדא has stopped anyway. Standing would cost him nothing extra.

phrases.english: He said to him: He is standing and praying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב חסדא is standing and praying.

steps.title: רב ששת stands too: 'From being good, do not be called bad'
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks to be stood up so he can pray too, explaining that one should not settle for less when doing better is easy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Stand me up too, and I will pray. 'From being good, do not be called bad.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת chooses to stand and pray even though his own view says standing is not required. The story ends with his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת never said walking is better, only that it is allowed. Since they had stopped anyway, standing was easy, and choosing the lesser way would look bad.

keyTerms.meaning: from being good, do not be called bad

steps.whatToRemember: Even by רב ששת, walking is only allowed. When standing is easy, it is better to stand: 'מהיות טוב אל תקרא רע'.
steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת did not change his mind. He still holds that standing is not required; he just chose the better way when it cost nothing.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: אוֹקְמַן נָמֵי לְדִידִי וַאֲצַלֵּי,
phrases.english: He said to him: Stand me up as well, and I will pray,
'From being good, do not be called bad.'
phrases.notes: A popular saying: if you can easily do the better thing, don't pick the lesser one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹקְמַן נָמֵי לְדִידִי וַאֲצַלֵּי מֵהֱיוֹת טוֹב אַל תִּקָּרֵא רַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב ששת reacts to the attendant's answer and closes the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Standing is the better way to say תפלת הדרך; even the one who allows walking stands when it is easy.

steps.title: How is הביננו different from תפלה קצרה?
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the משנה, the גמרא asks for the practical difference between הביננו and the תפלה קצרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between 'הביננו' and the short prayer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to two short prayers mentioned earlier in the sugya and asks how they differ in practice. The answer follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are short prayers, so they seem alike. The גמרא asks whether there is a real difference in halacha between them.

keyTerms.meaning: the short prayer said in a dangerous place

phrases.english: What is the difference between 'Grant us understanding'
phrases.notes: הביננו is the shortened שמונה עשרה discussed earlier, on the משנה's 'מעין שמונה עשרה'.

phrases.english: and the short prayer?
phrases.notes: This is the quick prayer the משנה gives for someone walking in a dangerous place.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין הֲבִינֵנוּ לִתְפִלָּה קְצָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves תפלת הדרך and returns to the משנה's short prayers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical halachic difference between הביננו and תפלה קצרה.

steps.title: הביננו: needs the first and last three, and counts as your prayer
steps.stepSummary: With הביננו you must say the first three and last three ברכות, and you do not repeat the prayer when you get home.
steps.simpleTranslation: With הביננו one must say the first three and the last three ברכות, and when he gets home he does not need to pray again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first side: הביננו is framed by the regular opening and closing ברכות of the עמידה, and it fully counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הביננו shortens only the middle ברכות into one. Since the beginning and end are complete, it counts as a real עמידה, so there is nothing to make up later.

keyTerms.meaning: the first three ברכות of the עמידה
the last three ברכות of the עמידה

phrases.english: With 'Grant us understanding', one needs to recite
the first three and the last three blessings,
and when he reaches his home
he does not need to pray again,

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲבִינֵנוּ בָּעֵי לְצַלּוֹיֵי שָׁלֹשׁ קַמָּיָיתָא וְשָׁלֹשׁ בָּתְרָיָיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First half of the answer to step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הביננו requires the first and last three ברכות and fully counts as the עמידה.

steps.title: תפלה קצרה: no framing ברכות, so pray again at home
steps.stepSummary: The תפלה קצרה needs neither the first nor last three ברכות, but you must say the full prayer once you get home.
steps.simpleTranslation: With the short prayer, one does not need the first three or the last three ברכות, but when he gets home he must pray again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the comparison: the תפלה קצרה is only a stand-in for an emergency, so the real עמידה must be said later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two prayers are opposites. הביננו is harder (it needs six extra ברכות) but counts fully. The תפלה קצרה is easier (no framing ברכות) but does not count, so it must be made up at home.
steps.whatToRemember: הביננו: first three + last three ברכות, and no need to pray again. תפלה קצרה: no framing ברכות, but you must pray the full עמידה when you get home.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the difference between a shortened version of the real עמידה and an emergency replacement that only holds you over until you can pray properly.

phrases.english: with the short prayer,

phrases.aramaic: לָא בָּעֵי לְצַלּוֹיֵי לָא שָׁלֹשׁ קַמָּיָיתָא
phrases.english: one does not need to recite either the first three
or the last three blessings,
but when he reaches his home
he needs to pray again.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּתְפִלָּה קְצָרָה לָא בָּעֵי לְצַלּוֹיֵי לָא שָׁלֹשׁ קַמָּיָיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the answer, set against הביננו in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תפלה קצרה needs no framing ברכות but does not count, so one must pray again at home.

steps.title: Final ruling: הביננו standing, short prayer either way
steps.stepSummary: The halacha is that הביננו must be said standing, while the תפלה קצרה may be said standing or walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: The halacha is: הביננו is said standing. The short prayer can be said either standing or walking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical bottom line of the comparison it just made between הביננו and the תפלה קצרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 16 and 17 we learned that הביננו counts as a real שמונה עשרה, and the תפלה קצרה does not. That is why הביננו needs standing like a full עמידה. The תפלה קצרה is more like an emergency prayer, so you may say it even while walking.

keyTerms.meaning: And the halacha is (the practical ruling)
A short version of שמונה עשרה that sums up the middle ברכות

steps.whatToRemember: הביננו is a real עמידה, so it needs standing. The תפלה קצרה is not, so walking is fine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling shows how the status of a prayer decides how it must be said.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: 'Grant us understanding' is said standing,

phrases.aramaic: תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה, בֵּין מְעוּמָּד בֵּין מְהַלֵּךְ.
phrases.english: the short prayer, whether standing or whether walking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the difference between the two prayers (steps 16 and 17) into a practical ruling about standing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הביננו requires standing. The תפלה קצרה may be said standing or walking.

steps.title: Rider on a donkey: get off if someone can hold the animal
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה, a ברייתא teaches that a rider should get off to pray if someone can hold his donkey. If not, he prays sitting on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If he was riding on a donkey...' The Rabbis taught: if someone was riding a donkey and the time for prayer came, and he has someone to hold his donkey, he should get down and pray. If not, he should stay seated where he is and pray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line of the משנה about a person riding a donkey. It brings a ברייתא that gives more detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the rider should get off, and only pray riding if he cannot. The ברייתא explains when 'he cannot' applies: when there is nobody to hold the donkey. This is the first opinion, and רבי will disagree with it next.

keyTerms.meaning: He should stay seated in his place

phrases.english: If he was riding on a donkey, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
If one was riding on a donkey
and the time for prayer arrived,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ מִי שֶׁיֹּאחַז אֶת חֲמוֹרוֹ —
phrases.english: if he has someone who will hold his donkey,
he should go down and pray;
and if not, he should sit in his place and pray.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה רוֹכֵב עַל הַחֲמוֹר וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, about praying while riding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rider gets off to pray if someone can hold the donkey. Otherwise he prays sitting on it.

steps.title: רבי: always pray sitting on the donkey
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that the rider always prays where he sits, because getting off would disturb his focus.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: either way, he should stay seated where he is and pray, because his mind is not settled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי argues with the first opinion of the ברייתא. He says the rider never needs to get off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion focused on whether getting off is possible. רבי focuses on the person's concentration. Someone in the middle of a trip is in a hurry, so getting off would make him anxious. He will pray better staying seated.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind is calm and settled

steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי' here is a specific person, רבי יהודה הנשיא, the one who put the משנה together. It is not a general title for 'a rabbi'.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ
phrases.english: Rabbi says: whether this way or that way,
phrases.notes: Whether or not there is someone to hold the donkey.

phrases.english: he should sit in his place and pray,
because his mind is not settled upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion inside the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rider always prays seated on the donkey, because concentration comes first.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: רבא, or some say רבי יהושע בן לוי, rules that the halacha follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say it was רבי יהושע בן לוי: the halacha is like רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא decides the argument from the ברייתא in favor of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of this ruling, a rider prays on the donkey even if someone is available to hold it. The גמרא is unsure who said the ruling, so it gives two possible names.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (it was someone else who said it)

steps.whatToRemember: A traveler on an animal may pray where he sits. Calm focus matters more than getting down.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
The halacha is like Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha follows רבי: the rider prays seated, whether or not someone can hold the donkey.

steps.title: Blind person or someone lost: aim your heart to Heaven
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone who cannot tell which direction to face should direct his heart toward his Father in Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a blind person, or someone who cannot figure out the directions, should direct his heart toward his Father in Heaven, as it says: 'And they shall pray to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about someone who does not know which way to face while praying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we face ירושלים when we pray. If someone cannot tell where that is, he is not stuck. He simply aims his heart at ה׳, and the פסוק shows that the main thing is praying to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: To figure out the directions (north, south, east, west)

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that facing ירושלים is meant to help focus the heart. When the direction cannot be known, the heart's focus on ה׳ is what remains.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: סוֹמֵא וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְכַוֵּין אֶת הָרוּחוֹת —
phrases.english: A blind person and one who is unable to figure out the directions
should direct his heart toward his Father in Heaven,
as it is said: 'And they shall pray to the Lord.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: סוֹמֵא וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְכַוֵּין אֶת הָרוּחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next topic in the משנה, which direction to face when praying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who cannot tell directions directs his heart toward ה׳, based on 'וְהִתְפַּלְלוּ אֶל ה׳'.

steps.title: Circles of direction leading to the ark-cover
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Wherever a person stands, he turns his heart one level closer: חוץ לארץ toward ארץ ישראל, ארץ ישראל toward ירושלים, ירושלים toward the בית המקדש, the מקדש toward the קודש הקדשים, and the קודש הקדשים toward the כפורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is outside the Land, he aims his heart toward ארץ ישראל. In ארץ ישראל, he aims toward ירושלים. In ירושלים, he aims toward the בית המקדש. In the מקדש, he aims toward the קודש הקדשים. In the קודש הקדשים, he aims toward the place of the כפורת. If he is behind it, he pictures himself as standing in front of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא from the last step keeps going. It explains where a person should aim his heart, depending on where he stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each level is one step closer to the center than the place where the person stands. The first four levels are each backed by a פסוק from שלמה's prayer at the dedication of the בית המקדש. The last levels, the כפורת and standing behind it, are taught without a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: He should aim or focus his heart
The Holy of Holies, the innermost room of the בית המקדש
The place of the כפורת, the gold cover on top of the ארון

phrases.english: If he was standing outside the Land —

phrases.aramaic: יְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: he should aim his heart toward ארץ ישראל,
as it says: "And they shall pray to You by way of their land."
If he was standing in ארץ ישראל —
he should aim his heart toward ירושלים,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהִתְפַּלְלוּ אֶל ה׳ דֶּרֶךְ הָעִיר אֲשֶׁר בָּחַרְתָּ״.
phrases.english: as it says: "And they shall pray to ה׳ by way of the city that You have chosen."
If he was standing in ירושלים —

phrases.aramaic: יְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: he should aim his heart toward the בית המקדש,
as it says: "And they shall pray toward this house."
If he was standing in the בית המקדש —

phrases.aramaic: יְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים,
phrases.english: he should aim his heart toward the Holy of Holies,
as it says: "And they shall pray toward this place."
If he was standing in the Holy of Holies —

phrases.aramaic: יְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית הַכַּפּוֹרֶת.
phrases.english: he should aim his heart toward the place of the כפורת.
phrases.notes: The כפורת is the gold cover on top of the ארון.

phrases.english: If he was standing behind the place of the כפורת —
he should see himself as if he were in front of the כפורת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא about which direction to face during תפלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person praying aims his heart one level closer to the center than where he stands, all the way in to the כפורת.

steps.title: All of Israel faces one place
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא sums up its rule. People east of the center face west, those west face east, those south face north, and those north face south. So all of Israel aims at one place.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it turns out: someone in the east turns to the west, in the west turns to the east, in the south turns to the north, and in the north turns to the south. All of Israel aims their hearts toward one place.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא draws its conclusion from the circles it just described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no single fixed direction like "always face east." The direction depends on where you stand compared to the center. The result is that everyone points inward toward the same spot.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out, as a result

steps.whatToRemember: The direction of תפלה is not one fixed compass direction. Everyone faces inward toward the קודש הקדשים, so all of Israel aims at one place.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think everyone faces east. Only someone standing west of ירושלים faces east. Someone standing east of it faces west.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of facing toward ארץ ישראל, ירושלים, and the מקדש during שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: It turns out that one standing in the east
turns his face to the west.
One in the west turns his face to the east.
One in the south turns his face to the north.
One in the north turns his face to the south.
It turns out that all of Israel
are aiming their hearts toward one place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical result of the circles described in step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All of Israel, wherever they are, face toward one center: the קודש הקדשים.

steps.title: A hint from שיר השירים: the hill all mouths turn to
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין, or some say רבי אבינא, brings a פסוק as a hint. He reads the word תלפיות as "תל שכל פיות פונים בו," the hill that all mouths turn toward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין (or רבי אבינא) said: Which פסוק hints to this? "Your neck is like the tower of דוד, built for תלפיות." That means the hill that all mouths turn toward.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a פסוק that supports the idea that all of Israel pray toward one place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He splits the word תלפיות into two parts: תל (hill) and פיות (mouths). So the פסוק describes the מקדש as the hill that every praying mouth turns toward. This supports the conclusion of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (the statement is said in someone else's name)
Read as תל + פיות: the hill of mouths

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי אֲבִינָא:
phrases.english: רבי אבין said, and some say it was רבי אבינא:
Which פסוק hints to this?
"Your neck is like the tower of דוד, built for תלפיות" —
a hill that all mouths turn toward.
phrases.notes: He is playing on the word: תל means hill and פיות means mouths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as support for the conclusion that all of Israel face one place.
steps.raayaObject: That all of Israel turn toward one place, the מקדש, when they pray.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שיר השירים 4:4, with the word תלפיות read as "the hill all mouths turn toward."

steps.title: Praying early before a journey
steps.stepSummary: Whenever שמואל's father and לוי wanted to set out on a trip, they prayed early. Later, when the time for קריאת שמע came, they said שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: When שמואל's father and לוי wanted to go out on the road, they would pray early. When the time for קריאת שמע came, they said it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic connected to travel. It reports what two אמוראים used to do before a journey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They prayed שמונה עשרה before they left, which was earlier than the usual time and before קריאת שמע. They said שמע later, on the road, once its proper time came. This reverses the usual order of שמע first and then תפלה, and that sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: To set out on the road
They would get up early and pray

phrases.english: שמואל's father and לוי,
when they wanted to set out on the road,
would pray early,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הֲוָה מָטֵי זְמַן קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע קָרוּ.
phrases.english: and when the time for קריאת שמע arrived, they would say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל וְלֵוִי, כִּי הֲווֹ בָּעוּ לְמִיפַּק לְאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about תפלה and travel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before a journey, one may pray early and say קריאת שמע later, at its proper time.

steps.title: Whose opinion did they follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא supports what שמואל's father and לוי did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like whom did they act?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short question. It sets up the next step, where the גמרא finds a source for their practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their practice was unusual, so the גמרא wants to find a תנאי source that backs it up. The question is not attacking them. It is looking for support.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose opinion does this follow?

phrases.english: Like whom did they act?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the practice in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view matches praying early and saying קריאת שמע later when traveling.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports doing מצוות early before traveling
steps.stepSummary: They followed a תנא in a ברייתא. That ברייתא says someone leaving early for a trip does שופר, לולב, and מגילה before he goes, and says שמע when its time comes. Likewise, someone leaving early by wagon or boat prays first and says שמע when its time comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: They followed this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: If someone got up early to travel, they bring him a שופר and he blows it, a לולב and he shakes it, a מגילה and he reads it. When the time for קריאת שמע comes, he says it. If he got up early to ride in a wagon or a boat, he prays, and when the time for קריאת שמע comes, he says it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It quotes a ברייתא that matches what שמואל's father and לוי did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets a traveler do the day's מצוות early, before he sets out. The case of the wagon or boat is the exact match: he prays early, and he says שמע later, when its time comes. That is exactly what the two אמוראים did.
steps.whatToRemember: A traveler may pray early before setting out and say קריאת שמע later at its proper time. A תנא in a ברייתא supports this.

phrases.english: Like this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches:
If he got up early to go out on the road,
they bring him a שופר and he blows it,
a לולב and he shakes it,
a מגילה and he reads it,
and when the time for קריאת שמע comes, he says it.

phrases.aramaic: הִשְׁכִּים לֵישֵׁב בַּקָּרוֹן אוֹ בִּסְפִינָה — מִתְפַּלֵּל,
phrases.english: If he got up early to ride in a wagon or a boat, he prays,
and when the time for קריאת שמע comes, he says it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27 by quoting a matching ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They followed the תנא of the ברייתא, who lets a traveler pray early and say קריאת שמע later at its proper time.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: always say שמע and then daven
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagrees with the first תנא of the ברייתא. In either case, the traveler should say שמע and then daven, so that גאולה is right next to תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Either way, he says קריאת שמע and then davens, so that he puts the redemption ברכה right next to the תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא now brings a second opinion. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says the traveler should not daven before leaving. He should say שמע and the עמידה together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תנא let the traveler daven early and say שמע later, which splits them apart. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר insists they stay together, even if that means davening on the road. His reason is the rule of סמיכת גאולה לתפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption: the ברכה after שמע that ends גאל ישראל
Going straight from the גאולה ברכה into the עמידה with no break

steps.confusionAlert: Here "תפלה" means the עמידה (שמונה עשרה), not davening in general.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Either way,
phrases.notes: Even the traveler in the cases just mentioned should not split שמע and davening apart.

phrases.english: he recites the Shema and then prays,
so that he puts redemption right next to prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion in the same ברייתא, arguing with the first תנא quoted in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a traveler should say שמע and then the עמידה together, to keep גאולה next to תפלה.

steps.title: What is the argument about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle the two תנאים are arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the root of the argument between the first תנא and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides want the traveler to daven properly. The גמרא wants to know which value each side puts first.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the underlying reason behind the disagreement between steps 28 and 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which principle divides the first תנא and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: Standing for the עמידה versus keeping גאולה next to תפלה
steps.stepSummary: The first תנא holds that davening standing is more important. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that putting גאולה right next to תפלה is more important.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds that davening standing is better. The other master holds that joining גאולה to תפלה is better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The two תנאים are weighing two good things, and each picks a different one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you daven at home before the trip, you can stand, but שמע ends up separated from the עמידה. If you wait and do both on the road, you keep them joined, but you may have to daven sitting in the wagon or boat. The first תנא picks standing, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר picks סמיכת גאולה לתפלה.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument is about priorities: standing for the עמידה (first תנא) versus going straight from גאולה into תפלה (רבי שמעון בן אלעזר).

phrases.english: One master holds that prayer while standing is better,
phrases.notes: This is the first תנא, who said to daven at home before leaving.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר מִסְמָךְ גְּאוּלָּה לִתְפִלָּה עָדִיף.
phrases.english: and the other master holds that joining redemption to prayer is better.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first תנא gives priority to standing during the עמידה. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gives priority to סמיכת גאולה לתפלה.

steps.title: מרימר and מר זוטרא daven early with a מנין before the lecture
steps.stepSummary: On the שבת of the festival, מרימר and מר זוטרא gathered ten men, davened, and then went out to give their public lecture.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר and מר זוטרא would gather ten men on the שבת of the festival and daven, and then they would go out to the lecture.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about two sages who had a busy schedule on a big שבת. They made their own early מנין so they could daven before giving the lecture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another case of davening at an unusual time because something else is pressing, like the traveler. They did not skip the מנין. They brought one together themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: A group of ten; a מנין
The Shabbat of the festival, when crowds came to hear a lecture

phrases.english: Mareimar and Mar Zutra
would gather ten men
on the Shabbat of the festival and pray,
and then they would go out to the lecture.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָרִימָר וּמָר זוּטְרָא הֲווֹ מְכַנְּפִי בֵּי עַשְׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the traveler to a new kind of time pressure: a big public lecture.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a lecture was coming, they gathered their own מנין and davened before it.

steps.title: רב אשי davens sitting with the צבור, then again standing at home
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי davened sitting, privately, along with the צבור. When he got home, he davened again standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי would daven with the צבור, by himself and sitting. When he came home, he would daven again standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how רב אשי handled the same kind of situation in a different way. This sets up the questions the רבנן ask him next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the צבור davened, רב אשי said his own תפלה quietly in his seat. That davening was not standing, so at home he davened again properly, standing. Standing matters to him, which ties back to the first תנא's priority.

keyTerms.meaning: As an individual; on his own

phrases.english: Rav Ashi would pray
with the congregation, as an individual, sitting.
phrases.notes: He was in the room with everyone, but he quietly said his own תפלה in his seat.

phrases.english: When he would come to his house,
he would pray again, standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי מְצַלֵּי בַּהֲדֵי צִבּוּרָא בְּיָחִיד מְיוּשָּׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second sage's way of handling the same busy-day problem from step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי davened sitting with the צבור and later davened again standing at home.

steps.title: Why not do what מרימר and מר זוטרא did?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ask רב אשי why he does not gather an early מנין like מרימר and מר זוטרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to him: Let the master do like מרימר and מר זוטרא!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge רב אשי's practice. They point to a simpler way that avoids davening twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he gathered an early מנין, he could daven once, standing and with ten, before the lecture. So why does he use his awkward two-step method?

keyTerms.meaning: Let the master do (a pushing suggestion)

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to him:
Let the master do like Mareimar and Mar Zutra!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן: וְלַעֲבֵיד מָר כְּמָרִימָר וּמָר זוּטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's practice from step 33 using the example of step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's practice of davening sitting and then again at home.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a better option: an early מנין where he can daven once, standing.

steps.title: It is too much trouble for me
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that gathering an early מנין would be too much of a burden for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The matter is burdensome for me.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why he does not copy מרימר and מר זוטרא. Their method is too much trouble in his situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer is practical, not a disagreement about halacha. Gathering ten men and davening before the lecture would make things too hard for him, so he uses his own method.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter is a burden for me

phrases.english: He said to them: The matter is burdensome for me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 34.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אשי could easily do what מרימר and מר זוטרא did.
steps.terutzMaskana: For him that method is too much trouble, so he davens with the צבור and again at home.

steps.title: Then why not daven early like שמואל's father and לוי?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן suggest another option: daven early, the way שמואל's father and לוי did before a trip.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the master do like שמואל's father and לוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן push again with a second idea. It comes from the story earlier on the daf about davening early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's father and לוי davened early and said שמע later when its time came (step 26). That would also let רב אשי daven once, standing, without gathering anyone.

phrases.english: Let the master do like Shmuel's father and Levi!
phrases.notes: This points back to step 26, where they davened early before setting out on a trip.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אשי rejects the first suggestion, the רבנן offer a second one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Davening early, as שמואל's father and לוי did, avoids both the burden and davening twice.

steps.title: I never saw older sages do that
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that he never saw sages older than himself act that way, so he will not rely on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I have not seen the rabbis who are older than us doing this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי turns down the second suggestion too. His reason is that the older sages did not practice this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof comes from what the elders actually did. Since the senior sages did not daven early like that, he does not treat it as the accepted practice. So his own method stays.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי rejects both options: an early מנין is too much trouble, and davening early was not done by the older sages. So he davens sitting with the צבור and again standing at home.

phrases.english: He said to them:
I have not seen the Rabbis
who are older than us doing this.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא חֲזֵינָא לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן קַשִּׁישֵׁי מִינַּן דְּעָבְדִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 36 and closes the רב אשי story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to the practice of older sages
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Davening early like שמואל's father and לוי is a fine option for רב אשי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The older sages did not do this, so רב אשי does not rely on it.

steps.title: The משנה: Three Views on Saying מוסף
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings three opinions on whether מוסף depends on a חבר עיר: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, the חכמים, and רבי יהודה quoting רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: מוסף is only said where there is a חבר עיר. The חכמים say: it is said with a חבר עיר and without one. רבי יהודה says in his name: any place that has a חבר עיר, the individual is exempt from מוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lays out three opinions about whether an individual must say מוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה ties מוסף to the community's group. The חכמים say everyone says מוסף, group or no group. רבי יהודה gives a second version of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view, focused on the individual living where a חבר עיר exists.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra (מוסף) prayer said on שבת, יום טוב and ראש חודש
A city's organized prayer group, a מנין

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different versions of the same תנא here. The first opinion and רבי יהודה's report both come from רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, so they sound alike. The גמרא is about to ask exactly that.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: MISHNAH: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
The additional prayer is not said
except with a city group.
phrases.notes: A חבר עיר is the town's organized group of ten that davens together.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
With a city group and without a city group.
Rabbi Yehuda says in his name:
phrases.notes: "His name" means רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם חֶבֶר עִיר —
phrases.english: Any place where there is a city group —
an individual is exempt from the additional prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין תְּפִלַּת הַמּוּסָפִין אֶלָּא בְּחֶבֶר עִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, moving from the story of רב אשי to the laws of מוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three views: מוסף only with a חבר עיר; מוסף either way; where there is a חבר עיר, the individual is exempt.

steps.title: Isn't רבי יהודה the Same as the First Opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks that רבי יהודה's version seems to say the same thing as the first version of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה: why record two versions that seem identical?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions link מוסף to the חבר עיר. If they mean the same thing, there is no point in listing רבי יהודה's version separately.

keyTerms.meaning: The first Tanna, the opinion stated first in the משנה

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא!
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Yehuda is the same as the first Tanna!
phrases.notes: The "first Tanna" here is the opening opinion of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the structure of the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two versions of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's opinion in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two opinions say the same thing, the משנה would not list them as different.

steps.title: The Difference: An Individual Where There Is No Group
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that they argue about an individual in a place with no חבר עיר: the תנא קמא says he is exempt, רבי יהודה says he is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: an individual not in a place with a חבר עיר. The תנא קמא holds he is exempt. רבי יהודה holds he is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows there is a real difference between the two versions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says מוסף only belongs with a group, so a lone person with no group never says it. רבי יהודה says the exemption only exists where a group is present, so a person with no group nearby must daven מוסף himself.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.confusionAlert: Reversal trap: רבי יהודה's version sounds more lenient ("exempt"), but for a person with no group nearby it is the stricter view. He is obligated.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
an individual not in a place with a city group.
The first Tanna holds he is exempt.
And Rabbi Yehuda holds he is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 39.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a practical difference (נפקא מינה) in a specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two versions seemed to say the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue about a lone individual where there is no חבר עיר: exempt according to the תנא קמא, obligated according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: no group, no מוסף. רבי יהודה: only a group in town exempts the individual. With no group, he must daven מוסף.

steps.title: The Halacha Follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא quotes רב חייא בר רב: the halacha follows רבי יהודה's version of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא said in the name of רב חייא בר רב: the halacha follows רבי יהודה, who spoke in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives the practical ruling on the משנה's argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling follows רבי יהודה. So where there is a חבר עיר, an individual is exempt from מוסף. Where there is none, he must say it himself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns the argument among the תנאים into a practical ruling about when an individual must daven מוסף.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Ḥinnana said
that Rav Ḥiyya bar Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: who said it in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the difference between the views is clear, the גמרא gives the ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Halacha follows רבי יהודה: an individual is exempt from מוסף only where there is a חבר עיר.

steps.title: Support from שמואל's Practice
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין agrees with the ruling and supports it from שמואל, who said he never davened מוסף alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין said to him: You spoke well, since שמואל said: In all my days I never davened מוסף as an individual.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא backs up the ruling with a proof from how שמואל acted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חייא בר אבין agrees with the ruling and starts to prove it from שמואל's own practice: שמואל says he never davened מוסף alone. His sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud, which explains exactly how his practice proves רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: You have spoken well, you are right

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin said to him:
You have spoken well,
as Shmuel said:
In all my days I have not prayed
the additional prayer as an individual

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling of step 41.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that halacha follows רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's own practice: he never davened מוסף alone.
